subject: HAWK at Zenith and Richmond
comment: Myself and many other parents use the crosswalk on Richmond road to bring our children to the daycare. Many cars do not see the flashing lights to slow down and stop and allow for crossing. subject: Fund HAWK on Richmond
comment: Hello, My child attends daycare in Salt Lake City at the intersection of Richmond road and Zenith Ave. Myself, and many of the other families, live near the area and will use the crosswalk to cross Richmond road. This crosswalk is very scary to cross as an adult, let alone with a small child in tow. Many drivers don't notice the flashing lights to slow down or stop for pedestrians. Having a HAWK in place so that pedestrians can control a stop light at the crosswalk on Richmond would help keep dozens of children and families safe. Please consider funding the placement of a HAWK at Richmond road and Zenith Ave in Salt Lake City. Thank you for your consideration, Haley Lemon

subject: flags
comment: "I hate intolerant people" "I judge you to be judgmental" "I can't stand how those people stereotype others" "If you were open-minded you would think like me" Quick takeaway: If love equals love, then hate equals hate. Evil exists in the world; however, most bigotry is little more than a good idea co-opted by a zealot. Intolerance in the name of God, patriotism or motherhood, may have been a legitimate focus of criticism during the last few decades; but the last election provided evidence of a tipping point where the general population will no longer be bullied into silence over blatant intolerance in the name of civil rights, feminism and gay rights either. Hate in the name of victimhood is not only still hate, but also the worst form of hate because the perpetrators should know better. It is the moral equivalent of a person who was abused as a child arguing that they have the right to be an abusive parent. Hate equals hate. For example: Would you name a street after a co-councilman who was sexually exploiting your underage runaway daughter? Of course not. Yet Harv Milk discusses in his own biography his sexual relationship with at least one 16-year-old runaway boy while Milk was in his mid-thirties. SLC dutifully performed Equality Utah's work and named 900 South after Milk, while ignoring the history of exploitation. Activists cannot simultaneously claim to support gay youth while actively throwing them under the bus. The sexist, orientation-phobic subtext is that gay boys have less value than straight girls. Providing a pass to Milk because of "the narrative" is precisely why the woke left is viewed by many as being the very thing it claims to despise. * Humans are capable of multiple emotions at the same time; a parent may be both happy and sad at the wedding of their child. Similarly, homosexuals and allies may simultaneously be supportive of gay rights advocacy while being appalled at activist intolerance preformed in their name. Just as many Caucasians reject the Klan and religious people reject violence in the name of God; many homosexuals actively disagree with the extremism of activist groups that are typically represented by the rainbow flag. The Human Rights Campaign, Equality Utah, etc. may be voices in the gay community, but they are emphatically not THE voice of all homosexuals. Groups such as Log Cabin Republicans or Gays Against Groomers (typified by media personalities such as Dave Rubin or Guy Benson) also have a legitimate voice outside the rainbow ghetto. The fundamental intolerance of identity politics is the belief that physical attributes/orientation inherently determine politics. Such a dogma is the antithesis of "diversity." The rainbow flag is NOT a decoration. It is a political flag, and it is a flag representing only portions of the homosexual population; to the exclusion/hostility towards others. While Salt Lake City may virtue bat signal with a rainbow lit clock tower or cutesy rainbow flags, the city is not credibly providing a middle finger protest of the legislature, it is providing a giant statement of contempt to its own residents who may or may not be homosexual but still have the audacity to reject child exploitation, reject criminalizing dissent (conversion therapy bans have been found by the courts to violate the first amendment and the supreme court is now hearing a Colorado court case). Many do not support the physical mutilation of children or support opposite genders being forced to share locker rooms, as well as other ideas endemic to the rainbow. Many reject the idea that some political flags should be imposed, while others banned. Many simply tire of the hypocrisy of those who cannot look in the mirror and realize that they, like a religious zealot chopping off heads in the name of God, have come to personify what they claim to despise. If Salt Lake City wants to be diverse, equitable and inclusionary, the simple answer is to stop being blatantly divisive, exclusive and intolerant. The little leftist who cried "you are a racist/sexist/homophobic/hitterbooger" seeking to vilify those who dare notice the duplicity, no longer have any credibility. While I applaud leaders for standing up for gays and lesbians; I am disappointed in those leaders who stomp on free speech when faced with bullying from gay activists under some garbled guise of exclusionary "inclusion"; I am disappointed in media who often merely parrot the bidding of the woke, rather than question their motives the same as they would with other groups; and I am specifically disappointed in gay activists who demand an acceptance they do not offer, making a mockery of their own demands for "tolerance". Too often, woke advocates think their victim status gives them the right to perpetrate, when in fact, it demands them the moral obligation to do better. When I drive by the City/County building and see the lights/flag, I think of my good friend who was serially gay abused in foster homes as a youth, (of which Equality Utah/SLC tacitly approves) who subsequently sought out "conversion therapy" (which Equality Utah seeks to criminalize) and is now happily married to a member of the opposite gender. Where is his flag? I emphatically believe that abuse should be confronted at all times. However, the great irony of identity (aka victim) politics is that if a person's identity is based upon their victim status, 1) the incentive is to never stop being a victim, otherwise they lose victim power (rather than attain actual empowerment) resulting in sore-winners and crybullies. 2) it incentivizes the intolerance towards non-approved victims, because they are a threat to power of the designed victims (aka the insensitivity towards my friend because he does not advance the narrative), and 3) it incentivizes the vilification of others in order to aggrandize victim power. Although the circumstances are different, SLC's non-political political victim flags are passive/aggressive to us-ass Societal levels. A world where tribes are designated by their oppressor/victim status based on identity group rather than actual behavior is dysfunctional. To paraphrase Orwell; Some "victims" are more "equitable" than others. A flag does not exist for my friend because he does not fit the "narrative" and he is not interested in being a perpetual victim. It is merely a matter of time before someone sues SLC's blatant duplicitous action of picking and choosing what residents are officially valued. As a SLC resident, would love to be a plaintiff because SLC clearly hates me because I dared to notice that identity politics, in their current form, thrive on perpetuating abuse, rather than ending it. The question is not whether the Utah State Legislature is wrong to seek political neutrality in public spaces; the question is how Salt Lake City can credibly pretend that it is diverse, equitable and inclusive to do otherwise. * Finally: Thank you for your service. Being an elected official is a thankless job where people mostly complain. I do recognize and commend the work you do. footnotes: * I don't have an inherent problem honoring flawed people, we all are. I have a problem with the piety of eliminating Columbus Day while ignoring flaws of the currently fashionable. Milk supported Jim Jones, * I agree with Equality Utah that conversion therapy has a low success rate and anything can be weaponized. My complaint is that the study of "damage" that I am aware of seemed suspiciously political, there are those who benefited, and Troy Williams opposed a legitimate legislative compromise that would ban all abusive therapies; presumably because gender conversion therapy has an even worse reticence rate, it involves actual physical damage and Equality Utah was clearly interested in criminalizing dissent, not saving gay youth. The final legislative action in response to Herbert/Cox executive action, was motivated by a need to define what conversion therapy isn't. * This letter was mostly written before news of threats. Violence and threats should always be condemned. One may strongly disagree with Trump, Israel or health care executives and still oppose violence against them. Unfortunately, fashionable violence is often rationalized as being "fiery but mostly peaceful" and hate hoaxes diminish legitimate outrage.

subject: TAKE ACTION NOW
comment: June 12, 2025 Dear Salt Lake City Councilmembers: Our community is appalled by the recent ICE raids in Los Angeles. As one statement put it, "What's happening in Los Angeles right now is not only morally reprehensible—it's legally indefensible..." We echo this condemnation and insist that Salt Lake City take action now to protect all residents. First, we demand that the Council adopt a binding sanctuary ordinance. The City must explicitly ban local cooperation with ICE: revoke any authorization to honor ICE detainers, and forbid sharing city data (e.g., arrest records, personal information, GIS mapping of undocumented residents) with federal immigration agents without a judicial warrant. ICE detainers are not binding by law, and detaining someone on an ICE detainer without a warrant violates the Fourth Amendment. Salt Lake City has full authority to ensure that police, jail officials, and other city staff do not comply with ICE detainers or searches except as required by valid court orders. Second, allocate emergency legal support for detained immigrants. Budget funds or coordinate pro bono attorneys so that anyone facing deportation has immediate access to counsel and translators. Publicly oppose any ICE enforcement actions or raids; pass a resolution formally condemning warrantless sweeps and reaffirming our commitment to due process. Direct the City Attorney to assist by filing or supporting legal challenges (such as amicus briefs or temporary restraining orders) against unconstitutional ICE policies. We should join other jurisdictions in defending immigrant families and preventing federal overreach. Finally, publicly refuse to enforce any part of the federal "Big Beautiful Bill." Pass a City resolution declaring that Salt Lake City will not implement any provisions of this legislation if it becomes law, and will not alter local policies under threats of federal funding cuts. Always call ICE raids what they are: armed kidnappings of workers and families with no due process. Our Council must ensure that Salt Lake City remains a sanctuary of justice and constitutional rights. It is extremely alarming that people are being held indefinitely in detention centers with no oversight, no due process, and nobody knows the conditions they are in or if any abuse is going on behind closed doors. Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter. We will be watching for your prompt action. Sincerely, Katrina Shore Concerned Salt Lake City Resident

subject: Prevent Unlawful Detentions and Refuse SLCPD Cooperation with ICE
comment: Dear Mayor Mendenhall and Salt Lake City Council, I'm a proud and engaged citizen of Salt Lake City, writing today with urgent concern about the safety of our communities here. Across the country this year, we've seen plainclothes, unmarked, and unaccountable agents raid private properties, harrass community members, and detain innocent people without warrants, accountability, or any semblance of the due process owed to us by law. These tactics amount to kidnapping, and Salt Lake City must not allow them to take place here. While I appreciate that SLCPD does not have a formal 287(g) agreement with ICE, your current policy leaves room for discretionary cooperatio, wherein SLCPD "may provide available support services" to ICE and other federal agencies, at a supervisor's discretion. This vague policy creates dangerous loopholes that can be exploited to use our City's resources to assist in ICE's illegal and violent activities. I am writing to share two demands that I know are supported by my neighbors and friends in SLC: 1. Refuse all SLCPD cooperation with ICE on civil immigration enforcement. We demand a firm and public commitment to codify this into city ordinance. SLCPD should never participate in or facilitate ICE raids, either directly or indirectly. 2. Treat abduction as the crime it is. At minimum, the City must refuse to enable or tolerate ICE's illegal tactics within our jurisdiction. If an individual is being harassed or abducted — regardless of the agency or alleged justification — SLCPD has a duty to treat it as a crime and respond accordingly. Let's be clear: being undocumented is not a criminal act; it is a civil classification that does not justify surveillance, harassment, or detention. Meanwhile, abduction without a warrant or lawful authority is illegal, and we have the opportunity, as a progressive and proud city, to lead the nation in its prevention. While I personally believe our country's legal approach to immigration is absolutely unjust an immoral, I am not asking for my city to break the law. I am asking for it to stand up for its most vulnerable populations, as it has often done in its proud history. So, I'm asking you directly: 1. Will you take steps to formally bar SLCPD from cooperating with ICE on immigration detentions? 2. Will you publicly commit to treating ICE-style detentions — without due process, identification, and/or warrants — as the criminal acts they are? We are watching. You will see our engagement in the streets and beyond until every measure has been taken to protect our beautiful communities. Please choose justice and act swiftly to protect the people of Salt Lake City. Sincerely, Lissa Reed Salt Lake City resident, district 5

subject: Request to fly flags at half mast with respect to Afa Ah Loo
comment: --------------------------- Original Message --------------------------- Subject: Request to fly flags at half mast with respect to Afa Ah Loo From: "Kurt Allen Fisher" <fisherkaj@jns.com> Date: Mon, June 16, 2025 12:06 am To: erin.mendenhall@slcgov.com Cc: citycouncil@slcgov.com letters@sltrib.com ------------------------------- June 16, 2025 Via Governmental Web Application Governor Spencer Cox Via Email erin.mendenhall@slcgov.com Salt Lake City Mayor Erin Mendenhall Request to fly flags at half mast with respect to Afa Ah Loo Governor Cox and Mayor Mendenhall, Thirty-nine-year-old Afa Ah Loo was shot and killed at the "No Kings" protest on June 15, 2025, in Salt Lake City. As a symbol of respect and as an aid to community mourning from this loss, this is to request that State Capitol and Salt Lake City and County Building flags be set at half-mast for two days, beginning by the end of business on Tuesday, June 17, 2025, until the end of the business day on June 19, 2025. Ah Loo was an innocent bystander exercising his peaceful right to assemble, and part of a crowd of 10,000 similarly non-violent Utahns. Regardless of the political motivations of the rifleman, a core issue is the chilling of the community's right of peaceful assembly. A unified governmental gesture that crosses political lines of lowering flags would bolster the community's healing from the transgression of that right. Given the national political divisions and the length remaining in the president's term, more large protests in Utah are certain. By lowering flags, you honor the memory of a fallen, ordinary Utahn caught in a divisive controversy of our times and reinforce that Utahns have the constitutional right of assembly free of fear of violence from any part of the political spectrum. Very Truly Yours, Kurt A. Fisher
